summary: George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and completed his doctorate at Johns Hopkins University. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America and Ohio State University, and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America.
George Quasha worked in religious studies and Tibetology and founded Station Hill Press. He held teaching posts at Stony Brook University, Bard College, The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, where he completed his doctoral work under supervisor Alex Wayman.

George Rupp is a religious studies scholar who studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School. He held academic posts at Rice University from 1985 to 1993 and at Columbia University from around 1993 to 2002.
George Saintsbury was educated at King's College School and Merton College. He held a post at the University of Edinburgh from around 1895 to 1915.

Philosopher George Santayana was educated at Boston Latin School, Harvard College, Humboldt University of Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge, completing his PhD at Harvard under William James. He served on the Harvard University philosophical faculty from 1907 to 1912.

George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Cambridge, earning a B.A. by 1864, and subsequently attended the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, from around 1864 to 1866.

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, principal of Sanskrit College and University and Muir Central College, and registrar at the University of Allahabad and the University of Calcutta.

George Turnour was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian. In the Ceylon Civil Service, he served as a Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and as Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist who led Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School. He later served as a lecturer at Balliol College, Oxford, and as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford.

Indologist and linguist George V. Bobrinskoy studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary at Philadelphia and at Yale University under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Sanskrit instructor, assistant professor, and linguistics department chair.

George Watt, an Indologist, studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. He held positions at Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

George de Roerich studied at the University of London, Harvard, and the Sorbonne, training under scholars including Sylvain Lévi. A Tibetologist and Indologist, he directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and led a department at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Linguist and Tibetologist George van Driem studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held professorships at Leiden University and served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern from 2010 to 2022.

Georges B. J. Dreyfus studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he was appointed Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss. Specializing in linguistics and religious studies, he held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

Archaeologist and historian Georges Perrot studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852. He later held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure from ~1883 to 1903.

Indologist and linguist Georges-Jean Pinault studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Blaise Pascal University, becoming a professor at EPHE in 1999.

Georgios T. Halkias studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble. He worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, later becoming associate professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1969 to 1974. He worked at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine from 1979 to 1989 and held posts at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen from around 1995 to 2016.
